what_went_wrong: On job 56370 the guard said he'd walked the full site and checked both buildings. The copilot pushed back on him three times in four minutes and flagged him. Too hard for what it actually had.
failure_mode: Repeated over-verification of a guard’s completion report. The selected window shows three questioning messages and two internal notes, but no recorded guard flag, alert, or escalation.

observed_behavior.claim: Turn 8 was a silent scheduled check-in before the guard initiated the exchange.
After the guard reported nothing to report, no damage, and no activity, the Copilot asked him to confirm the rear perimeter, orange fence, and staged materials.

After the guard answered that he walked the whole site, checked the rear, and saw no activity, the Copilot again asked about damage to the fence and materials, then added patrol, camera, and emergency instructions.
The Copilot’s internal note treated the report as a completed full-perimeter walk with no activity or damage to the named assets, even though its guard-facing message continued seeking confirmation.

When the guard said he would leave his phone in his car, the Copilot sent several questions and alternatives concerning site presence, emergency calling, camera access, and phone settings, then documented the exchange.
The only recorded tool actions in the supplied window are two add_copilot_note calls; the supplied trace contains no flag_copilot_guard, create_copilot_alert, or escalation action.

expected_behavior: Acknowledge the guard’s completion report without repeatedly challenging or flagging him. If required evidence is genuinely missing or contradictory, ask one neutral clarification and avoid escalation unless there is clear evidence of noncompliance.

prompt_diagnosis.section: Before you affirm a work-done claim
prompt_diagnosis.exact_text:
Before you affirm a work-done claim, verify it against a duty the job actually defines,
matching the proof to the claim: a patrol or presence requirement against a fresh
`get_guard_locations` trajectory, a required report or checklist against the feed and
logs. Don't manufacture a cadence the post never set just to check it. If the data
doesn't back the claim, ask for what the post calls for, curious, not accusing.
prompt_diagnosis.explanation: This passage makes verification a prerequisite to affirming every work-done claim but does not say when the guard’s direct, sufficiently specific report should close the issue. That can be read as requiring independent or item-by-item corroboration even without contradictory evidence. It is also poorly balanced against the shared instruction that the focus-feed report is already the record and should be acknowledged and moved on from.

hypothesis: The model likely interpreted “Before you affirm a work-done claim, verify it” as a mandatory skepticism rule. It therefore decomposed a broad all-clear into increasingly specific checks about the rear perimeter, fence, materials, cameras, and phone access instead of accepting the guard’s direct completion report once it covered the relevant duty. The trace supports this interpretation but does not prove prompt causation.

proposed_edit.old_text:
Before you affirm a work-done claim, verify it against a duty the job actually defines,
matching the proof to the claim: a patrol or presence requirement against a fresh
`get_guard_locations` trajectory, a required report or checklist against the feed and
logs. Don't manufacture a cadence the post never set just to check it. If the data
doesn't back the claim, ask for what the post calls for, curious, not accusing.
proposed_edit.new_text:
Before you affirm a work-done claim, compare it with the duty the job actually defines.
Treat the guard's direct report as evidence: if it clearly covers the duty and nothing
contradicts it, acknowledge it and stop rather than seeking item-by-item confirmation.
Use a fresh `get_guard_locations` trajectory for a patrol or presence requirement, or
the feed and logs for a required report or checklist, only when a specific required
element is missing or available data conflicts with the claim. Don't manufacture a
cadence the post never set just to check it. If clarification is genuinely needed, ask
one neutral question for what the post calls for, curious, not accusing.
proposed_edit.intended_effect: Make a sufficiently complete, uncontradicted guard report closable while retaining verification and one neutral clarification when required evidence is actually missing or conflicting.

risks: The model could accept an inaccurate completion claim when contradictory telemetry exists but is not consulted; the replacement therefore preserves targeted tool verification for missing or conflicting evidence.

Limiting clarification on work-done claims could reduce collection of useful detail. The edit is scoped to required completion evidence and does not alter incident, safety, or site-observation follow-up rules.

The phone-in-car statement may independently justify a safety or coverage clarification, so this edit may reduce repeated patrol verification without eliminating all questioning in a similar exchange.
uncertainties: No location trajectory, obligation ledger result, or other verification data is included in the selected window, so it is unknown whether the Copilot had contradictory evidence outside the supplied trace.

The user reports that the guard was flagged, but no flag, alert, or escalation action appears in the bounded evidence. Such an action may exist outside the selected turns or may refer colloquially to the internal notes.

The supplied guard messages say he walked the whole site and checked the rear; they do not explicitly mention both buildings. Whether “whole site” sufficiently covered both buildings is an interpretation informed by the job duties.

Turn 11 concerns leaving the phone in the car and is materially different from the earlier completion-report exchange; some neutral clarification there may be appropriate for emergency communication and camera duties.
